paragraphs.dominant_move: open with injured residents and blocked transport links
justify assumptions and notation before modeling
name AHP and normalization as the weighting interface
move from ideal selection to image-based rough siting
close with schedules, sensitivity, strengths, and conclusions
quantify hurricane severity and human impact
introduce rotor-wing delivery and road observation roles
ask how model quality will be judged
pair road coverage and completion time with duration

global_organization_chain: The summary opens with blocked post-hurricane access, names medicine delivery and road reconnaissance, then compresses AHP weighting, greedy fleet selection, rough siting, realistic packing, pixel siting, timetable construction, sensitivity, and final recommendations.
The introduction converts disaster context and heterogeneous drones into three measurable success criteria, making the later AHP stage predictable before technical detail begins.
Assumptions and notation bound range, charging, packing, weather, terrain, storage, communications, entities, units, and output symbols before those choices become hidden inside formulas.
The report fixes three containers from hospital reach and charging flexibility, then uses the flow diagram to route that deployment count into criterion weighting and packing.
AHP keeps time, medicine amount, and reconnaissance separate; three normalization subsections produce f(D), g(n), and h(x) before CE combines them.
CE drives a marginal greedy fleet whose ideal volume balance produces a 411-day upper bound, and the prose explicitly hands that optimistic state to a realistic packing stage.
B/D delivery-return radii and B transfer range become a map overlay; Areas A-C then assign hospital responsibility, D drones, and medicine types across containers.
The 70-percent initialization, allocation rules, external packing oracle, and bisection replace ideal counts with realized container inventories and utilization.
Rough areas, realized ranges, roads, and populated places become standardized raster features whose weighted maxima yield the three exact coordinates.

Exact coordinates and packed inventories become a five-slot-per-day timetable; the sensitivity section then revisits range and AHP interfaces before conclusion and the HELP letter reassemble the decision.

The final pass records equation, fleet, code, coordinate, schedule, sensitivity, cross-reference, caption, and provenance warnings without replacing positive language, organization, model, equation, or visual evidence.

main_argument_chains.claim: The fleet objective is constructed from three stakeholder-facing criteria before any drone is selected.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use CE only after repairing units, Dmax/Nmax definitions, weight provenance, and proxy-to-operation validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: Greedy selection converts CE into an ideal fleet and an optimistic medicine-duration bound.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the result as a heuristic ideal state until iteration traces, global bounds, dimensional accounting, and body-code constants reconcile.

main_argument_chains.claim: Range geometry and hospital roles produce three connected rough container areas.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the rough areas as heuristic candidate domains until projection, terrain, energy, and formal facility-location comparisons are supplied.

main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not freeze exact locations until body/code weights, in-place mutation, source rasters, CRS, transform, and B-longitude conflict are resolved.

main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the operational communication chain while requiring a conservation-tested schedule, global uncertainty, unified coordinates and counts, and source provenance.

warnings.warning: The extracted text reports lambda_max=3.0183, while focused visual inspection can plausibly be read as 3.0153. The ambiguity must be resolved from the source matrix rather than silently normalized.

The delivery-time expression mixes route distance/speed with T0 declared in minutes, while the prose later replaces heterogeneous route, speed, payload, and charging terms by inverse drone count without a dimensional reconciliation.

The displayed Dmax numerator uses 3Vc-3(Vh-120Vm), whose parentheses and sign can add rather than reserve medicine volume. The expression, units, and intended three-container accounting require reconstruction.

The ideal result is B121/D54/H3, the appendix initializes a different D constant, the real packing contains B99/D42/H3, and the conclusion states B121/D42 while omitting H; these are distinct states and cannot be merged.

The displayed 411-day numerator appears to use one Vc while the surrounding calculation concerns three containers, and its denominator notation does not clearly separate daily package counts from package volumes.

The prose presents a bisection over a retained percentage beginning at 70 percent, but the appendix first hard-codes a 339-day fleet scale. The searched quantity and reported 359-day endpoint are therefore not reproduced by the printed code.
The body assigns road/highway weight 0.6 and populated-place weight 0.4, but appendix A.4 implements 0.4 and 0.6 respectively, so the reported coordinates lack a unique scoring specification.
The raster-scoring function modifies road and city arrays in place while evaluating candidates. Later scores can therefore depend on candidate and function-call order rather than only on location.
The five-day 359-day claim is not accompanied by a complete inventory, payload, route, charge-port, battery, turnaround, and terminal-state conservation ledger for every timetable cell.
A maximum 33.3-percent change in D-drone count is characterized as small and stable. A local one-factor plot does not establish end-to-end robustness or justify that interpretation.
The appendix uses hard-coded normalizers 394 and 256*52.67. Their derivation and consistency with the displayed Nmax and Dmax formulas are not demonstrated.
The appendix fixes 339 in the B/D scaling formulas even though the body reports 411 ideal days and 359 realized days, leaving the bisection target and final fleet unreconciled.

Convert flight specifications and the common 80-percent factor into three map radii.
Show hospital reach, coastline exclusion, inter-container transfer, and Areas A-C.
Show one realized cuboid arrangement for each cargo container.
Bind every B/D/H and MED count to containers A-C and report utilization.
Combine rough areas, service ranges, roads, populated places, and candidate geometry before exact pixel scoring.
Report the three latitude-longitude outputs used downstream.
Locate the selected container points against roads and populated places.
Encode first-day medicine assignments, origins, destinations, and transfer actions.
Show the second-day state and hand off to the repeated A/C departure cycles through day five.
Compare exact locations under loaded-distance factors 0.775, 0.8, and 0.825.
Compare B count, D count, and support days under one-factor weight changes.
Return the selected container and hospital points to a recognizable geographic context.

request_body_guard.transport_finding: HTTP 413 was an nginx ingress rejection caused by the accumulated serialized request, dominated by repeated image/base64 payloads and amplified by large patches and compaction carryover. Q127 therefore used eight JPEG proxies no larger than 450000 bytes, at most one image per tool call, no original full-page PNG, no complete session JSONL or base64 output, and text/hash checks after the eighth proxy.
